Elliotts Way.road: Narrow estate road, no centre line, block-paved parking courts and drives off it, no humps seen.
Elliotts Way.note: 1990s estate of orange-red brick terraces, semis and detached houses with porch canopies and contrasting brick bands, plus three-storey brick flat blocks with garages; open-plan fronts and paved parking.

Patrick Road.road: Narrow residential road, no centre line, single yellow line in places, on-street parking.
Patrick Road.note: Mixed street: three-storey modern red-brick townhouses with integral garages behind hedges at the south end, Victorian red-brick bay-fronted terraces and white-rendered cottages with low white walls at the north end; one view mostly fence and trees.

Wolsey Road.road: Residential road, no centre line, give-way markings at junctions, on-street parking, some driveways.
Wolsey Road.note: North end is Victorian/Edwardian red-brick semis and short terraces with bays and slate roofs, some rendered; south end has 1970s-80s brown/orange brick houses with tile roofs behind fences and big hedges.

Rufus Isaacs Road.road: Quiet cul-de-sac estate road, no centre line, no markings, drives and open lawns.
Rufus Isaacs Road.note: 1990s cul-de-sac of red/orange brick detached houses with integral garages and brown concrete tile roofs, plus a buff brick flat block and big three-storey red brick block; one view black, one mostly a side wall.

The Willows.road: Estate road with tight bends, no centre line, double yellow lines at the junction, block-paved drives.
The Willows.note: 1980s estate of red-brick two-storey semis, short terraces and detached houses with small gabled porch canopies, garages and open-plan paved fronts and shrubs.

Kingfisher Place.road: Not seen from a road: both views are a user photosphere on the Thames towpath.
Kingfisher Place.note: Only a riverside towpath photosphere: a stepped 1980s red-brick terrace with dark sawtooth roofs and dark-framed glazed balconies, behind hedges; other view is just the river.

Priory Avenue.road: Two-lane residential road, no centre line, parked cars both sides, some driveway entrances.
Priory Avenue.note: Edwardian red-brick villas with gables and bays, a mock-Tudor gabled flat block and a red-brick chalet-style cottage with dormers; low red-brick walls with piers and tall fences, one view mostly fence and a skip.

Prospect Street.road: A4155 main road through the centre: two lanes, centre line, mini-roundabout with painted white disc at the Church Street/Bridge Street end, zebra/give-way markings, buildings right on the pavement.
Prospect Street.shops: South end (towards Church St) is mostly shops on both sides, perhaps 60% of frontage there; north end residential. Shopfronts are two- and three-storey Victorian terraces: dark green fascias and dark green awnings on white-painted buildings, black/dark grey fascias, full-width plate glass below. Upper floors of shops mostly white-painted brick or render with sash windows, some plain red brick with bay windows. A large 1980s red-brick office/flats block (4 storeys, slate mansard with dormers, carriage arch) and Victorian red-brick 'Church House' with blue door at the corner.
Prospect Street.note: Victorian two- and three-storey terraces fronting the pavement: red brick and painted (white, one blue-painted) cottages to the north, a row of small shops with green and black fascias and awnings near the mini-roundabout, with a big 1980s red-brick mansard block opposite.

Church Street.road: A4155 main road, two lanes with centre line, traffic lights and pedestrian crossing at the junction, petrol station forecourt, buildings and tall brick garden walls on the pavement.
Church Street.shops: Few shops in these views, maybe 20-30% of frontage: a white-painted pub with a long black fascia board and gold lettering; a grey/stone Victorian gothic two-storey building with a dark shopfront and big windows on the corner; a red petrol-station canopy. Shops are ground floor of 2-storey buildings with plain dark fascias, no awnings seen.
Church Street.note: Historic main street: Georgian red-brick house with sash windows and arched window, a 1980s red-brick mansard office, white-painted pub and cream low cottages with clay tile roofs, a gabled grey-brick Victorian corner block, and long red-brick garden walls under trees.

Cardinal Close.road: Narrow cul-de-sac, no centre line, a turning circle with a planted island and yellow kerb lines, parking bays and garage blocks.
Cardinal Close.note: 1970s close of red/orange brick two- and three-storey flats and town houses with dark-stained boarding, green-door garage courts, tall beech hedges and shrubbery that hide most buildings.

Cromwell Road.road: Narrow residential street, no centre line, cars parked both sides on the road, some single yellow line.
Cromwell Road.note: Victorian red-brick terraces with white-painted ground-floor bays, contrasting yellow/white brick bands and slate roofs, tiny front gardens behind low red-brick walls; a 1930s semi and a 1990s brick semi near the north end.

Westfield Road.road: Residential through road, no centre line, double yellow lines in places, parking on one side, junction with a bollard island at the south end by the recreation ground.
Westfield Road.note: Long Victorian terraces of red brick with yellow-brick bands, some painted white, with bays, slate roofs and dormers; tiny front gardens behind low walls, hedges and picket fences; south end opens onto trees by the park.

Chester Street.road: Narrow street, no centre line, parking both sides; the east end meets Prospect Street with give-way lines and zebra-hatched markings.
Chester Street.shops: Only at the Prospect Street end, about 10% of the street: a corner shop with a red fascia and red canopy, a green fascia shop opposite, and the Prospect Street parade beyond (3-storey Victorian red-brick and white-painted gabled buildings with grey/dark fascias and plate-glass fronts).
Chester Street.note: Victorian red-brick terraces with white painted bays and slate roofs, plus Edwardian semis with gables and timber detailing, behind low brick walls and hedges; corner shops where it meets Prospect Street.

Promenade Road.road: Quiet road by the river meadows, no centre line, grass verges with railings.
Promenade Road.note: Four-storey 1990s-2000s red-brick flat blocks with white window bands and balconies set in lawns behind hedges and railings; second view is mostly hedge and trees.

Abbotsmead Place.road: Private access road with brick gate piers and double yellow lines at the entrance.
Abbotsmead Place.note: Modern three/four-storey retirement-style flats in red brick and white render with steep gables, behind brick piers and shrubs; the other view is solid trees.

Waller Court.road: Short cul-de-sac with a grassed island, no markings, parking bays in front of houses.
Waller Court.note: 1990s close of red/orange brick terraced and semi houses with brick bands, small gabled porch canopies (one with mock-Tudor gable) and brown tile roofs, open-plan lawns and parking.

Rectory Road.road: Narrow street, no centre line, parked cars both sides.
Rectory Road.note: Victorian terraces of red brick and silver-grey Reading brick with red-brick dressings, white-painted bay windows, gabled end houses and slate roofs; small front yards behind low walls.

Crendon Court.road: Estate road, no centre line, single/double yellow lines, parked cars.
Crendon Court.note: Only one view loaded and it resolves to The Willows: 1980s red-brick two-storey houses and a three-storey red-brick flat block with shrubs; may not show Crendon Court itself.

South Street.road: Narrow street, no centre line, double yellow lines, a church car park off it.
South Street.note: Victorian red-brick chapel/church hall with arched windows and slate roof, red-brick and white-painted terraces beyond, a white low building with a red fascia, behind low walls and hedges; one view partly blocked by roadworks barriers.

Short Street.road: Narrow street, no centre line, double yellow lines at the corner, parking on street.
Short Street.note: Victorian red-brick and buff/stone-faced terraced houses with slate roofs behind low brick walls with piers, plus a 1970s two-storey red-brick flat block set back behind grass.

Oxford Street.road: Narrow street, no centre line, parked cars both sides, raised doorsteps with steps.
Oxford Street.note: Long plain Victorian red-brick terraces with yellow brick bands and lintels, slate roofs and chimneys, front doors up steps behind tiny yards and low brick walls; a modern three-storey red-brick infill at one end.

Harley Road.road: Two-lane road, no centre line, double yellow lines and a give-way junction, service yard with bins and a car park.
Harley Road.note: 1980s two-storey red-brick sheltered flats with some white rendered gables behind a low red-brick wall and lawn, and a red-brick house beside a car park/service yard.

Tamesis Place.road: Estate road, no centre line, kerbed junction with Patrick Road, garage/bin store blocks.
Tamesis Place.note: Only one view loaded: 1990s three-storey orange-red brick flat blocks with gables and brick bands, a brick bin store, and houses beyond; hedges along the far side.

North Street.road: Narrow back street, no centre line, rear service alley with garages off it.
North Street.note: Victorian red-brick terraces with yellow-brick bands and slate roofs, one white-painted, tiny yards behind low walls; other view is a rear alley of brick walls and lock-up garages.

St Martins Precinct.road: Pedestrian precinct, no road: block-paved square with trees, low seating walls, a market stall area with red parasols.
St Martins Precinct.shops: Nearly all shops/cafes (about 95%). Two-storey 1960s-70s precinct blocks of buff/yellow brick over continuous ground-floor shopfronts: full-height glazing in light frames, a deep flat fascia band (grey/dark blue-grey on most, light grey/cream on the cafe), a flat-roofed canopy along the frontage, outdoor tables. One upper storey of offices/flats above shops with plain strip windows.
St Martins Precinct.note: Paved pedestrian shopping precinct with trees and red market parasols, lined by two-storey buff-brick 1960s/70s shop blocks with continuous glazed shopfronts and grey fascia bands; both views are a user photosphere.

St Stephens Close.road: Cul-de-sac, no centre line, parking court and garage block, no markings.
St Stephens Close.note: 1980s close of red-brick two-storey starter homes and three-storey brick flats with green garage doors, open-plan lawns and shrubs and a parking court.
